bracket: [Textbook answer-key error, plus an unphysical given. The wires are in series with the same length and cross-section, so each extends in proportion to \(1/Y\); with the values AS PRINTED that gives tungsten \(3.2445\) mm and steel \(0.005516\) mm, which sum to exactly the \(3.25\) mm the question states. The printed key gives the steel extension as \(0.0052\) mm, and its two figures sum to \(3.2492\) mm — they do not reach the total the stem itself supplies, which is what identifies the steel value as the wrong one. Separately, the given \(Y_{\text{Tungsten}} = 3.40 \times 10^{8}\) N/m\(^{2}\) is not tungsten: the real value is about \(3.4 \times 10^{11}\) N/m\(^{2}\), STIFFER than steel, so physically the tungsten wire must extend LESS than the steel one rather than some six hundred times more. It is also forty times below lead, the least stiff metal in this chapter's own Table 6.1. The question is solved as printed; with the physical value the extensions would instead be \(1.204\) mm and \(2.046\) mm.]
